question: Should this hardened installer support provider-specific external dependencies, and if so should it expose a narrowly scoped npm-only mechanism, a broader apt-plus-npm mechanism, or require operators to install them separately?
rationale: The request adds privileged package-management and supply-chain surface, while the current installer intentionally has a fixed bootstrap path; source inspection cannot safely determine the intended security and support boundary.

options.title: Keep dependencies explicit
options.body: Document that operators install optional provider CLIs separately under the intended user account, leaving the hardened installer dependency-minimal.

options.title: Add a scoped npm list
options.body: Support a documented, non-root list of npm packages for the OpenClaw user while keeping OS packages fixed and trusted repositories unchanged.

options.title: Add apt and npm extensibility
options.body: Introduce separate package lists only with explicit repository, pinning, privilege, and failure-policy design plus security review.

recommendation.title: Keep dependencies explicit
recommendation.body: Document that operators install optional provider CLIs separately under the intended user account, leaving the hardened installer dependency-minimal.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available history signal for the existing Node/pnpm bootstrap path affected by this policy choice.
